description.p: YouTFast is a small native YouTube client built with Rust, egui and libmpv. Search and play videos, keep a local library and optionally use a YouTube account through the system credential store.
This is an early-stage unofficial client, not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

The top-bar bell opens a notifications popup, Settings are centred with an index of their groups beside them, controls fade into their hover and pressed looks, and on Linux any installed font can draw the interface. Adds a step-by-step install guide for each system.

Sizes the watch page player to each video's aspect ratio and widens Up next and theater mode to use the window. Comment timestamps seek within the current video, and web links in descriptions and comments open in the default browser.
Maintenance release: the source is split into focused crates and takes rustypipe from a pinned fork instead of a vendored copy. No change to the application's behaviour, files or settings.

Adds sending videos to TVs through Google Cast and YouTube's TV link (DIAL/Lounge, or a TV code), with optional SponsorBlock skips on the TV, and browser-style video tabs. Shows channel avatars on Home's recommendations.

Adds system interface fonts with an Inter option and a customizable sidebar. Reduces History, Home, Notifications and comment rendering costs, improves keyboard access and account reliability, and refreshes the project website.

Adds Settings → About with release notifications and SHA-256-verified minor/patch auto-updates, configurable video buffer size, audio-only playback mode, History sync options, and Flathub/Winget/Homebrew channel manifests. Improves page scrolling, keyboard navigation, and the compact mini player.

Adds Spanish, French, German and Italian interface languages, channel links and an optional miniplayer while scrolling. Improves startup and thumbnails, fixes channel tabs and counts, and keeps video rendering clipped while scrolling.
First release with native playback, local library, optional accounts and reliability and privacy protections.
